ai.description: This 30–40 mm frog is brown with dark mottling. It features a pointed snout, prominent toe pads, and distinct, fleshy femoral glands. It inhabits high-altitude streams in the Anamalai Hills.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Anamallai Night Frog is best distinguished by its distinct, elongated, and pointed snout that projects significantly beyond the lower jaw, unlike most other congeners.
ai.habitat: The Anamallai Night Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen rainforests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at 1,000–2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Anamallai Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden in rock crevices or under leaf litter during the day to avoid predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Anamallai Night Frog breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 20–50 eggs on wet rocks or vegetation, which undergo direct development without a tadpole stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Anamallai Night Frog is endemic to the Anamalai Hills in the Western Ghats, spanning the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Anamallai Night Frog produces a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard from rocky stream beds in the dense rainforests of the Western Ghats.
